initiatives.name: Net Zero Transition Plan 2024-2050
initiatives.summary: Beazley published its first Transition Plan in 2024 setting ambitions through end of 2026 with the goal of reaching net zero by 2050, covering Scope 1 and 2 emission reduction targets and broader Scope 3 objectives, including a 1.5-degree decarbonisation pathway for 2024-2034.

evidence.title: 50% reduction in normalised operational GHG emissions vs 2019
evidence.summary: Beazley achieved a 68.4% reduction (exceeding its 50% target) in normalised (per FTE) operational GHG emissions compared to its 2019 baseline, driven largely by reduced business travel emissions.
evidence.quote: Our market-based GHG emissions normalised for Beazley's full-time equivalent (FTE) (including contractors) were 1.67 tonnes carbon dioxide equivalent (tCO2e/ FTE) in 2025. This equates to a reduction of 68.4% when compared to the 2019 normalised baseline... This reduction continues to be in line with the target we set for a 50% reduction in emissions against a 2019 baseline of 5.30tCO2e/ FTE.

evidence.title: Climate transition plan update with new Scope 1 & 2 targets
evidence.summary: Beazley is updating its climate transition plan with revised emissions targets expected to be set at the May 2026 Board meeting, and is aligning sustainability metrics in its 2026 LTIP awards to these new targets. Current LTIP sustainability targets include Scope 1 & 2 emissions reduction trajectory, gender balance, and workforce diversity representation.
evidence.quote: As discussed on page 50, the Company is in the process of updating the climate transition plan with revised targets expected to be set at the May 2026 Board meeting.

evidence.title: Net Zero Transition Plan 2024-2050

initiatives.name: Bermuda Insurance Entity and ART Market Entry
initiatives.summary: Beazley is establishing a new insurance carrier in Bermuda to access specialist reinsurance and alternative risk transfer (ART) markets, with initial focus on Property Treaty and plans to expand into cyber ILS, captives and ART structures. The Board approved deployment of $500m of capital ($100m regulatory capital) to build out the platform, targeting $400m in written premiums by 2030.
